div.div:
Interconnect
Outer IP 10.0.0.4 → 10.0.1.10, UDP 4789
VXLAN VNI 50001 (the tenant's L3 VNI)
Inner Eth LEAF-4 router MAC → LEAF-BORDER router MAC
50:00:00:04:00:08 → 50:0a:00:00:1b:08 · inner TTL 63

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 402px; height: 1px; padding-top: 490px; margin-left: 370px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;

display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 762px; height: 1px; padding-top: 660px; margin-left: 10px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Where the inner MACs come from: every host route is an EVPN type-2 with two labels (L2 VNI + L3 VNI 50001), two route targets and a Router MAC community. LEAF-BORDER has no VLAN 20, so it uses only the routed half: a /32 in TENANT1 and LEAF-4's router MAC.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 762px; height: 1px; padding-top: 755px; margin-left: 10px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: var(--ge-adaptive-fg, #000000); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Cold destination: if LEAF-BORDER has no ARP entry for SERVER-11, LEAF-4 has only the /24 type-5 route, LEAF-BORDER must ARP and the first packet is dropped. After that, a /32 type-2 route takes every later packet straight through.
